title: Russian attacks leave a third of Kyiv without heating and over one million homes without power
body:
On 31 December 2025 UN News reported on attacks across Ukraine since 26 December that damaged civilian infrastructure and left parts of the country without electricity, heating and water as temperatures fell below zero. The UN humanitarian office (OCHA) reported nearly 100 civilian casualties during the period.

A large-scale attack on Kyiv on 27 December killed and injured several people and damaged energy facilities, homes, a preschool and a university dormitory. An energy company reported that more than one million homes in and around Kyiv lost power, and roughly one-third of the capital's population was left without heating. The same wave of attacks affected Chernihiv, Dnipro, Donetsk, Kharkiv, Kherson, Sumy and Odesa.

Power was restored to nearly 750,000 households in Kyiv and about 350,000 in the surrounding Kyiv region, but heating and electricity remained disrupted by emergency and scheduled outages. Humanitarian partners set up warming tents offering shelter, food, phone charging and basic assistance. The World Health Organization said Ukraine accounted for about 42 percent of attacks on health care recorded globally in 2025. Of more than 1,000 attacks on health facilities worldwide that year, 561 occurred in Ukraine, causing 19 deaths and 201 injuries, and a health facility in Izmail in Odesa region was damaged over the weekend of the attacks.
